newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: IMF urges transparency in Zimbabwe privatisation.
newsitem.headline: IMF urges transparency in Zimbabwe privatisation.

text.p: An International Monetary Fund official called on Zimbabwe on Monday to implement its unfolding privatisation programme in a transparent way, saying its success required the confidence of local and foreign investors.

IMF Southern African divisional chief Michael Nowak told a news conference the programme -- which state officials say will initially cover around 40 enterprises from cotton gins to steel plants -- should be built on consensus.
He was commenting on a controversial deal signed in September between the southern African state and a Malaysian company which many Zimbabweans and Western countries charge appeared underhand.

President Robert Mugabe has defended the pact -- under which Malaysian power producer YTL Corp Bhd would take a 51 percent stake in the privatisation of Hwange Thermal Power Station by investing Z$6 billion (U.S.$568 million) -- as above board and told Western critics "to go to hell".

Before the signing of the letter of intent, Zimbabwe's Electricity Supply Authority (ZESA) had invited bids and six foreign firms had been shortlisted with a British company at the top of the list while YTL was at the bottom.
Nowak said his organisation -- whose funding is crucial for a five-year economic reform plan Zimbabwe plans to launch this year -- had no problem if some deals were reached on political grounds.

"Our requirement is transparency," he said. "The public is entitled to know the value of the assets to be sold in order to maintain transparency in the privatisation process and this calls for broad-based consensus on the issue."
